identity.captured_title: You are the Deep Research source-base reviewer for NebulaMind's galaxy-evolution wiki rebuild. Queue item 01 of 20 Core review: Kennicutt, Robert C. Jr. & Evans, Neal J. II (2012), Annual Review of Astronomy and Astrophysics, volume 50, "Star Formation in the Milky Way and Nearby Galaxies." Known review identity to confirm, not merely repeat: DOI 10.1146/annurev-astro-081811-125610; arXiv 1204.3552; ADS bibcode 2012ARA&A..50..531K. Mission purpose Build a large, authoritative, advisory source base from this review so three independent methods can later build galaxy-evolution wiki pages from zero. Extract the review's own bounded synthesis and harvest the important primary papers it cites. This is not live-wiki prose and authorizes no database, trust, claim, evidence, deployment, publication, or account mutation beyond this one Deep Research run. Temporal boundary - The source base for this item is the 2012 review and primary literature it actually cites. - Do not introduce post-2012 papers as if the review cited them. - If a later source is useful only to detect a correction, place it in DO_NOT_USE_UNVERIFIED and state that it is outside this item's citation-harvest boundary. Scientific scope 1. Definitions and efficiencies of star formation from cloud to galaxy scales. 2. Star-formation-rate tracers and calibrations: ionizing/recombination lines, UV, infrared, radio, X-ray where relevant, hybrid indicators, timescales, dust attenuation, metallicity, IMF, stochastic sampling, and spatial-scale limits. 3. Initial mass functions only insofar as they control SFR conversions and stellar-population inferences. 4. Star-formation laws: integrated and resolved Kennicutt-Schmidt relations; HI, H2, total gas, and dense gas kept distinct; surface-density thresholds; disk versus starburst regimes. 5. Milky Way and nearby-galaxy molecular clouds, cloud lifetimes, efficiencies per free-fall time, dense-gas thresholds, clustering, and environmental variation. 6. Feedback, turbulence, gravitational instability, cloud formation/destruction, and theoretical interpretations, each labeled as observation, model, or review synthesis. 7. Known review-era tensions and unknowns. Do not retrofit conclusions from later literature. Composite citation identity rule Treat author + year + title + journal + DOI + arXiv + ADS bibcode as one identity. Every identifier supplied in a usable row must resolve to the same physical paper. A DOI, arXiv ID, or bibcode that resolves to a different real paper is contamination, not partial success. If exact identity cannot be confirmed, quarantine the item as UNCITED_NOT_USABLE. It is acceptable to omit an identifier type genuinely absent from the authoritative record; never guess one. Evidence hierarchy - Use the review as orientation and synthesis. - For every load-bearing finding, debate position, and number, include at least one important primary source that the review cites. - Prefer foundational or representative primary measurements over derivative summaries. - Keep observational results, calibrations, and theoretical/model claims epistemically distinct. - Preserve sample, tracer, IMF, metallicity, spatial-resolution, redshift, and conversion-factor boundaries. - Do not use the review's citation count or authority to rescue an overbroad claim. Return exactly these eight sections. ## 1. Review identity and scope map Confirm the review's composite identity. Then list its major sections/themes and what each can and cannot support for a galaxy-evolution evidence base. ## 2. Established findings At least 12 entries, IDs [REV01-E01], [REV01-E02], ... Each entry: - role: established - epistemic_type: observation|calibration|theory|review_synthesis - atomic finding - scope/boundary - review basis: section/topic and, where available, page/figure/table - confidence note - source keys: review plus at least one harvested primary source ## 3. Open debates and tensions At least 8 entries, IDs [REV01-D01], [REV01-D02], ... Each entry: - role: debate - debate_topic - competing positions - why unresolved as of the review's 2012 boundary - measurement/model/sample boundary - source keys representing more than one side where available ## 4. Key measurements and calibrations At least 8 entries, IDs [REV01-N01], [REV01-N02], ... Each entry: - role: measurement - metric or calibration and value/range - sample, tracer, instrument/method, spatial scale, and IMF - systematic caveat - primary source keys Do not blend incompatible IMF choices, gas phases, apertures, or SFR timescales. ## 5. What remained unknown in 2012 At least 6 entries, IDs [REV01-U01], [REV01-U02], ... Each entry: - role: future - gap - why it mattered - observation/model needed - review and primary source keys defining the gap ## 6. Primary-citation harvest Harvest 40-80 important primary papers actually cited by Kennicutt & Evans 2012. Balance the harvest across: - SFR indicators and calibrations; - resolved and integrated star-formation laws; - HI/H2/total/dense-gas measurements; - Milky Way and nearby molecular clouds; - IMF and stellar-population conversion assumptions; - turbulence, gravity, efficiency, and feedback models; - dwarf/low-metallicity and starburst boundaries. One physical row per source. Exact row format: [REV01-P001] Authors (year, journal) | title=<exact title> | DOI:<verified DOI if available>; arXiv:<verified ID if available>; ADS:<verified bibcode> | role=measurement|calibration|debate|theory|caveat|future | review_locator=<section/page/figure/table or topic-level locator> | one-line claim boundary Every harvested row must have an exact title, ADS bibcode, and every available reconciled DOI/arXiv identifier. Do not concatenate rows. Do not cite web pages, search snippets, theses, conference abstracts, or later papers as primary harvest items. ## 7. DO_NOT_USE_UNVERIFIED List every unresolved, cross-wired, outside-date, secondary-only, or overbroad item. Exact form: UNCITED_NOT_USABLE | proposed source or claim | unresolved/cross-wired identifier or locator | reason Include any claim that treats depletion time as a guaranteed future clock, conflates HI/H2/total/dense gas, treats one SFR calibration as IMF- or metallicity-independent, or converts a model mechanism into observational prevalence. ## 8. Review and source identity ledger First give the verified review row, then repeat one concise identity row for every usable primary source key. Exact row format: SourceKey | Authors (year, journal) | DOI:<doi if available>; arXiv:<id if available>; ADS:<bibcode> | role=review|measurement|calibration|debate|theory|caveat|future | one-line boundary Self-check before returning: - review identity matches Kennicutt & Evans 2012 across DOI/arXiv/ADS; - at least 12 established, 8 debates, 8 measurements, 6 unknowns; - 40-80 unique primary-citation rows actually cited by the review; - every claim source key exists in the final ledger; - every supplied DOI/arXiv/ADS tuple names one physical paper; - no post-2012 paper is promoted as a review-cited primary source; - no AGN-centered result is promoted as a core finding; - DO_NOT_USE_UNVERIFIED is present; - final line exactly: REVIEW_BASE_01_DR_COMPLETE_REFERENCE_ONLY Advisory source discovery only. Do not write live-wiki prose and do not authorize any mutation.
